title: Unexpected fallback to lower tier during Dedicated capacity saturation causing customer misroutes
creator: Arjun Patel
description:
Summary:
A production customer reported multiple requests that should have routed to their Dedicated pool (dedicated-eu-42) were served by a lower-tier hosted model (hosted-medium) in eu-west-1 during a period of elevated load. This exposed data to a non-dedicated environment and significantly degraded performance and tail latency for the customer.

Observed impact:
- Several customer requests failed SLOs and had increased P95 latency (~3x) because hosted-medium lacked pre-warmed KV caches and had different quantization settings.
- Customer raised an escalation citing privacy and SLA breach.
- Affected tenants span both Hosted->Dedicated routing and Dedicated->Private fallbacks in mixed deployments.

Initial timeline (UTC):
- 2026-03-10 01:12: Service monitoring alerted high queue lengths on dedicated-eu-42 GPU pool.
- 2026-03-10 01:14: Smart router began sending fallback traffic per policy.
- 2026-03-10 01:15–01:45: Significant fraction of requests went to hosted-medium rather than other Dedicated pools or region-appropriate fallbacks.
- 2026-03-10 02:05: Customer support escalated after audit showed non-dedicated processing.

Reproduction steps (dev cluster):
1. Configure tenant routing policy with primary dedicated pool (dedicated-eu-42) and fallbacks: dedicated-eu-43, dedicated-eu-44, hosted-medium-eu-west-1, private-onprem-uk.
2. Simulate a burst that raises dedicated-eu-42 occupancy > 95% and inject a short-lived capacity-update event (delta event delivery delay emulated).
3. Observe router decision logs for requests: some candidates from the hosted registry were selected even though dedicated-eu-43 was healthy.

Root cause (summary):
- Race between asynchronous capacity-update events and candidate list merge: when a Dedicated pool emits a saturation event, the router fetches fallback candidates from two registries (dedicated registry and hosted registry). Due to a bug in the candidate-merge comparator, candidates originating from the hosted registry were scored using a different key-space (score tuple: [availability_flag, -creation_ts, region_affinity]) while dedicated candidates used [availability_flag, priority_score, region_affinity]. This inconsistency allowed hosted candidates with slightly newer creation timestamps to outrank dedicated candidates that had lower priority_score but were region-compatible.
- Additionally, the routing cache TTL was 30s and a stale cache entry with an out-of-date preferred-order occasionally prevented immediate re-evaluation after pool state changed.
- The combination of inconsistent comparator semantics across registries + stale cache produced repeated misroutes during short saturation windows.

Why this escaped tests:
- Unit tests covered comparator behavior per registry but not cross-registry merges.
- Integration tests simulated saturation but used deterministic event ordering; the race condition appears only when capacity-update and registry-sync events interleave with real network jitter.

Temporary mitigation applied (2026-03-10 03:00 UTC):
- Deployed a hotfix to increase routing cache eviction frequency for dedicated routing keys from 30s -> 3s for affected tenants (safety-limited rollout).
- Added a reactive policy to prefer same-source candidates when source_priority met threshold (temporary tweak).
- Notified affected customers and created customer-facing incident timeline.

Proposed permanent fix (high level):
1) Unify comparator semantics: ensure candidate score tuple is normalized across all registries to [availability_flag, source_priority, priority_score, region_affinity, -creation_ts].
2) Make candidate-merge operation idempotent and atomic with respect to capacity-update events (use versioned pool state and CAS on routing decisions).
3) Reduce cache TTL for routing entries that include Dedicated pools, and add event-driven invalidation on capacity state changes.
4) Add cross-registry integration tests that fuzz event ordering and simulate network jitter; add a regression test that reproduces the race.

Rollout plan:
- Patch PR opened: runtime#3284 (see attachments). Change includes comparator normalization, cache TTL change (config flag), and new unit + integration tests.
- Canary: deploy to staging -> 5% of production routing decisions (traffic split) for 12 hours with telemetry gating (model-source mismatch rate, unintended-hosted-fallbacks, P95 latency per tenant).
- If gating shows <0.1% increase in mismatch and no customer complaints, expand to 50% then full rollout over 24–48h.
- Immediate rollback path documented in the PR and runbook (see attachments).

Monitoring & alerts to add before full rollout:
- Alert if model_source != expected_source for >0.05% of requests for *any* tenant in a 10m window.
- Alert if fallback candidate chosen outside of configured source whitelist for a tenant.
- Dashboard: routing-decision-lag, candidate-merge-latency, cache-staleness-by-key.

Longer-term follow-ups:
- Expand routing simulation harness and add nightly fuzzing.
- Add SLA-level telemetry that logs tenant->source mapping per request for audits.
- Revise docs: routing/fallback-policy semantics and operational runbook.

Stakeholders & communications:
- Notified CS and Legal on 2026-03-10 (privacy exposure risk).
- Weekly follow-up with affected customer scheduled; preparing data exports for audit.

updates: 2026-03-11: Investigated logs with infra. Found inconsistent score tuples across registries; reproduced race locally by delaying registry-sync events.
2026-03-11: Drafted comparator normalization and added unit tests for cross-registry merges. Opened feature branch and PR runtime#3284.
2026-03-12: Hotfix cache TTL change applied to affected tenants; immediate reduction in misroutes observed (~90% drop). Monitoring dashboards added.
2026-03-13: PR under internal code review. Security & privacy teams flagged need for customer audit exports before full rollout; coordinator assigned.
